MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures

**Document ID:** MRMA-SRP-2021  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Approval Date:** 01 March 2021  
**Next Review Date:** 01 March 2022  
**Owner:** MRMA Central Scheduling Office  
**Applies to:** All MRMA staff, contractors, and authorised rail infrastructure maintainers operating on Mallee Rail Maintenance Authority (MRMA) managed track.

---

**1. Purpose and Scope**

This procedure defines the standard rules for planning, submitting, approving, and reporting all track maintenance activities on MRMA-controlled corridors. It applies to routine, periodic, and emergency maintenance work, including but not limited to grinding, tamping, ballast regulation, rail defect management, vegetation control, and structure inspections.

The Mallee Rail Maintenance Authority founding charter states established_year 1998. Record status: historical. That charter remains the governing document for the Authority’s functions and is referenced throughout this procedure. The Scheduling and Reporting Procedures are subordinate to the charter and to any state or Commonwealth rail safety legislation applicable at the time of work.

These procedures are mandatory. Any deviation requires written approval from the Central Scheduling Office (CSO) at least five working days before the proposed activity, except in the case of a declared emergency per Section 6 of this document.

---

**2. Definitions and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| CSO | Central Scheduling Office, MRMA |
| TS | Track Section (numbered corridor segment) |
| WON | Work Order Number |
| PO | Possession (track closure for maintenance) |
| IP | Inspection Period |
| SRP | Scheduling and Reporting Procedures (this document) |
| STMP | Seasonal Track Maintenance Plan |
| RSO | Regional Scheduling Officer |
| FPO | Field Possession Officer |
| RWP | Roadway Worker Protection |

TS numbers refer to the fixed track section boundaries published in the MRMA Track Register, latest revision. No TS boundary may be altered except by formal survey and re-registration through the CSO.

---

**3. Scheduling Hierarchy and Planning Calendar**

Maintenance scheduling follows a four-tier calendar. Each tier is a prerequisite for the next.

**3.1 Annual Plan (Tier 1)**

The Annual Plan is compiled by the CSO no later than 15 October for the following calendar year. The Plan is derived from:

- The Seasonal Track Maintenance Plan (STMP) for the relevant year.
- Defect data from the previous 12 months.
- Known seasonal constraints (e.g., fire danger periods, harvest traffic, flood-prone sections).
- Available budget and crew allocations.

The Annual Plan is distributed to all Regional Scheduling Officers (RSOs) by 01 November. RSOs must confirm receipt within five working days.

**3.2 Quarterly Work Programme (Tier 2)**

Each RSO submits a Quarterly Work Programme to the CSO by the 15th day of the month preceding the quarter (i.e., 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December). The programme lists all planned WONs, proposed dates, TS references, and resource requirements.

The CSO reviews each programme for conflicts with other regions, possession availability, and weather outlook. Approved programmes are returned within ten working days with a status of Approved, Approved with Conditions, or Returned for Amendment.

**3.3 Weekly Schedule (Tier 3)**

Weekly Schedules are prepared by RSOs no later than Thursday 1400 for the following week (Monday–Sunday). The schedule must include:
Schedules are submitted in the standard CSO template. Handwritten or partially completed schedules are returned unprocessed.

**4.2 Conflict Resolution**

Where two or more regions request the same possession or plant resource, the CSO resolves the conflict in the following order of priority:

1. Safety-critical defect repairs (as defined in the Defect Management Manual)
2. Time-critical seasonal works (e.g., fire season mitigation)
3. Works that have been deferred from a previous week
4. All other programmed works

The CSO records the reason for each conflict decision in the weekly conflict log. Decisions are final and are not subject to appeal at the scheduling stage.

**4.3 Late Submissions**

Weekly Schedules received after Thursday 1400 are considered late. The CSO will process late schedules only where the work is safety-critical or where a delay would cause a breach of an inspection period (IP). All other late submissions are moved to the following week. The RSO concerned is notified by email within two working hours of the missed deadline.

---

**5. Possession Management**

**5.1 Possession Request Process**

All possession requests are submitted through the CSO possession portal. Requests must be lodged no later than 14 days before the proposed date, except for emergency possessions which follow Section 5.4.

A request must specify:

- PO number (auto-generated by the portal)
- TS and km limits
- Date and start/end times
- Type of possession (full closure, single line, or occupation on hand-signalling)
- Reason for possession
- Name and contact of the FPO responsible

Central Scheduling Office open_hours are 06:00-18:00 in the operational manual. Record status: current.

**5.2 Approval**

The CSO assesses each request against the current Weekly Schedule, planned maintenance windows, and any known passenger or freight commitments. Approval is granted in writing through the portal. Verbal approvals are not valid.

Where a request is for a possession longer than 8 hours on a main line, the CSO must also obtain written approval from the Manager Network Operations before the possession is confirmed.

**5.3 Cancellation and Variation**

Cancellations or variations to an approved possession must be lodged at least 48 hours before the scheduled start, unless the change is required for safety reasons. The CSO will confirm receipt and update the possession register. Possessions that are cancelled without notice are recorded in the RSO's performance metrics.

**5.4 Emergency Possessions**

Emergency possessions are those required to address a sudden loss of integrity (e.g., broken rail, washout, signal failure). The FPO may call the CSO directly at any hour. The CSO will open a possession record and advise the RSO and Network Operations immediately. The normal 14-day notice does not apply, but the emergency possession must be documented in the weekly conflict log and reviewed by the CSO within five working days.

---

**6. Central Scheduling Office Hours and Contact**

**6.1 Operating Hours**

Central Scheduling Office open_hours are 06:00-18:00 in the operational manual, and this remains the current standard for all routine scheduling and reporting contact. The CSO is staffed continuously within these hours on all weekdays, including public holidays that fall on weekdays. Outside these hours, the CSO phone diverts to the Network Operations duty desk, which can page the on-call CSO for emergency possessions only.

**6.2 Contact Channels**
**6.2 Contact Channels**

All routine correspondence with the CSO must be directed through the Scheduling Portal. Emails sent to generic inboxes are not monitored for scheduling requests. The portal accepts attachments up to 25 MB per file, and the CSO recommends PDF or native Excel formats.

For urgent clarifications during business hours, the CSO can be reached on extension 4410 or 4411. The CSO does not accept possession requests by phone; these must be lodged through the portal per clause 5.1. The duty desk contact for after-hours emergencies is recorded in the Network Operations directory.

**7. Maintenance Delay Report**

**7.1 Purpose and Scope**

The Maintenance Delay Report (MDR) provides a standard record of any maintenance activity, or lack thereof, that results in a delay to a scheduled passenger or freight service. The MDR is the primary source of data for the Monthly Performance Review and for the annual audit of maintenance windows. All RSOs, FPOs, and contracted maintenance providers must submit an MDR for any delay exceeding 3 minutes, measured from the booked departure time of the affected service.

**7.2 Submission Deadline**

Maintenance Delay Report submission_deadline is 2023-11-30 per reporting policy. Record status: current. This deadline applies to the final consolidated MDR for the November 2023 reporting period. Individual MDRs for specific incidents must be lodged within 5 working days of the incident occurring. The consolidated report aggregates all individual entries into a single file for the CSO's review.

The 2023-11-30 deadline is the current controlled entry in the reporting calendar. It supersedes the previous consolidated deadline of the last working day of the month, which was replaced to align with the new financial reporting cycle. Any MDR received after 17:00 on 2023-11-30 will be recorded as late, and the RSO will be notified for inclusion in the performance metrics.

**7.3 Content Requirements**

Each MDR must include the following fields:

- Date and time of the delay event
- Service number and line
- Track section (TS) and kilometrage
- Duration of the delay in whole minutes
- Cause code (from the current Cause Code List, Appendix B)
- Description of the maintenance activity in progress
- Name and signature of the person responsible for the activity
- Any corrective action taken to restore service

Where a delay is caused by a lack of maintenance (e.g., a failed inspection that was not performed), the MDR must state this explicitly and include the scheduled inspection date.

**7.4 Review and Acceptance**

The CSO reviews each MDR for completeness within 3 working days of receipt. If the report is incomplete, the CSO returns it to the submitter with a list of missing fields. The submitter must correct and resubmit within 2 working days. Unresolved MDRs are escalated to the Manager Network Operations.

The CSO maintains a register of all MDRs, including late submissions and resubmissions. This register is used to verify that the consolidated report contains all individual entries.

**8. Field Observation Protocol**

**8.1 General**

The Field Observation Protocol (FOP) is a companion document to these procedures. It defines the standards for recording observations of track, signalling, and overhead conditions during routine patrols and inspections. Where a conflict exists between the FOP and these procedures, these procedures take precedence for scheduling and reporting matters.
Observations must be entered into the Field Observation Database (FOD) within 24 hours of the patrol's completion. The CSO runs a weekly validation check on FOD entries; entries that fail validation are returned to the observer with a reason code. Common reasons include missing kilometrage, incorrect route code, or a condition code that is not current.

**8.4 Adverse Weather and Exceptional Conditions**

Where an observation is made under adverse weather conditions (e.g., heavy rain, high wind, or extreme heat), the observer must note this in the remarks field of Form FOP-1. The presence of adverse weather does not change the recording standards, but it may affect the priority assigned to a follow-up action. The CSO will flag observations made under adverse weather for review by the relevant RSO within 2 working days.

Exceptional conditions, such as a suspected structural fault, a signal failure, or an obstruction on the line, must be reported immediately by telephone to the Network Operations Centre (NOC) in addition to being recorded on Form FOP-1. The time of the telephone report must be noted on the form. The NOC will assign an incident number, which must be referenced in any subsequent maintenance or delay report.

**9. Regional Maintenance Forums**

**9.1 Purpose and Scope**

The Regional Maintenance Forums (hereafter "the Forums") are the principal mechanism for coordinating maintenance activities across regions and for reviewing performance against the AWP. The Forums provide a structured opportunity for RSOs, the CSO, and representatives from the NOC to discuss upcoming work, resolve conflicts, and share lessons learned. Attendance is expected for all RSOs and the CSO, or their nominated deputies. Deputies must be briefed on the current status of all items on the forum agenda before attending.

**9.2 Frequency and Scheduling**

Regional Maintenance Forums meeting_frequency is quarterly on the meeting calendar. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry in effect as of the date of this procedure. The quarterly cadence is set to align with the financial reporting periods used in the AWP and the consolidated reporting cycle described in Section 7. The CSO issues the schedule of forum dates for the coming year no later than 30 November of the preceding year. The schedule is published in the AWP and on the MRMA intranet.

Where a forum date falls on a public holiday, the forum is moved to the next working day. The CSO will notify all attendees of any change at least 10 working days in advance. Forums are not normally rescheduled for other reasons; if a forum must be cancelled due to an operational emergency, the CSO will convene a special session within 15 working days of the cancellation.

**9.3 Agenda and Papers**

The CSO prepares the agenda for each forum. The agenda is issued to all attendees at least 5 working days before the forum date. Standing agenda items include:

- Review of actions from the previous forum
- Update on the AWP status, including any changes to scheduled work
- Review of consolidated MDRs and late submissions
- Review of field observation outcomes, including any safety flags
- Discussion of resource availability and conflicts
- Any other business raised by attendees

Papers for the forum must be submitted to the CSO by 12:00 on the working day 3 days before the forum date. Papers submitted after this deadline are not guaranteed to be circulated before the forum and will be tabled as late papers. The CSO maintains a register of late papers for performance monitoring.

**9.4 Minutes and Action Items**

The CSO appoints a minute-taker for each forum. Minutes are to be issued within 5 working days of the forum date. The minutes must record:
**9.4 Minutes and Action Items (continued)**

The minutes must record the date, time, location, and list of attendees for the forum. For each agenda item, the minutes must note the discussion summary, any decisions made, and the action items arising. Each action item must include the responsible person or team, the required completion date, and the reference to the relevant AWP activity or MDR where applicable.

The CSO maintains the action item register. The register records the status of each action item as either Open, In Progress, Completed, or Overdue. The register is reviewed at each forum as a standing agenda item. Action items that remain open for more than two consecutive forums are escalated to the relevant Regional Manager and the Director of Maintenance Coordination.

Minutes are published on the MRMA intranet within 10 working days of the forum date. Minutes are retained in accordance with the MRMA Records Management Policy (document S05-02).

**Section 10: Consolidated Monthly Data Reports (MDRs)**

**10.1 Purpose and Scope**

This section defines the procedures for the preparation, submission, and consolidation of Monthly Data Reports (MDRs) across all regions. MDRs are the primary mechanism for reporting track condition, maintenance activity, and resource usage to the Central Scheduling Office. The procedures apply to all Regional Maintenance Managers, Maintenance Coordinators, and any staff responsible for submitting data.

**10.2 Report Content and Format**

Each MDR must be submitted using the standard MDR template, available on the MRMA intranet. The template requires the following sections:

- Track condition summary, including any defects identified and their severity rating
- Maintenance activities completed during the reporting month, referenced by AWP activity ID
- Resource usage, including labour hours, plant hours, and material quantities
- Any safety incidents or near misses
- Any changes to scheduled work, with reasons for the change

The MDR template is to be completed in full. Where a section is not applicable, the field must be marked as "N/A" rather than left blank. The CSO will return incomplete MDRs to the submitting region for correction.

**10.3 Submission Deadlines**

MDRs are due by 12:00 on the fifth working day of the month following the reporting month. The CSO issues a monthly reminder to all submitting regions two working days before the deadline.

Late submissions are recorded in the late submissions register. The register is reviewed quarterly by the CSO and reported to the MRMA Executive. Regions with more than two late submissions in a financial year are required to provide a written explanation to the Director of Maintenance Coordination.

**10.4 Consolidation and Review**

The CSO consolidates all regional MDRs into the Consolidated Monthly Data Report (CMDR). The CMDR is issued within 10 working days of the MDR submission deadline. The CMDR is distributed to the MRMA Executive, all Regional Maintenance Managers, and the Safety and Standards team.

The CMDR includes a summary of key indicators, including:

- Total kilometres of track inspected
- Number of defects identified, by severity
- Percentage of scheduled maintenance activities completed on time
- Total labour and plant hours used
- Any safety incidents or near misses

The CMDR is reviewed at the monthly scheduling meeting described in Section 7. Any anomalies or data quality issues identified during consolidation are raised with the relevant region for clarification.

**11. Data Analysis and Reporting**

**11.1 Purpose of Analysis**

This section defines the analytical procedures applied to maintenance and inspection data collected under the Field Observation Protocol (MRMA-FOP-001) and the Monthly Data Report (MDR) process described in Section 10. The purpose of this analysis is to support evidence-based scheduling decisions, identify emerging risks to track condition, and provide the MRMA Executive with a consistent basis for resource allocation.

**11.2 Track Condition Index (TCI)**

The Track Condition Index is the primary metric used to summarise the physical state of each track section (TS) across the network. The TCI is calculated monthly by the Central Scheduling Office (CSO) using defect data submitted in regional MDRs.

The TCI for a track section is a weighted composite score derived from the following inputs:

- Number of defects identified during the reporting month, by severity rating (Critical, Major, Minor)
- Kilometres of track inspected within the section
- Age of the most recently completed major maintenance intervention (e.g., resurfacing, grinding)
- Number of temporary speed restrictions (TSRs) in force at the end of the reporting month

The weighting factors are reviewed annually by the CSO and the Safety and Standards team. The current weighting matrix is reproduced in Appendix C of this document.

A TCI score is calculated for each track section and is expressed on a scale of 0 to 100, where a higher score indicates a better condition. A TCI below 40 is considered a trigger for review. Track sections with a TCI below 40 for two consecutive months are placed on the list of candidate sections for major maintenance intervention at the next annual planning cycle.

**11.3 Contractor Availability Index (CAI)**

The Contractor Availability Index is a scheduling metric that measures the proportion of contracted maintenance resources that were available for work during a given month, relative to the contracted baseline.

The CAI is calculated as follows:

CAI = (Actual available plant and labour hours / Contracted baseline hours) x 100

The CAI is reported for each major contract package and for each region. The CSO uses the CAI to:

- Identify recurring shortfalls in contractor availability that may affect the delivery of the Annual Works Program (AWP)
- Support decisions on whether to reschedule non-critical work to months where availability is expected to be higher
- Inform the procurement of supplementary plant or labour where the CAI falls below 90 for two consecutive months

The CSO produces a monthly scheduling performance report, which is an input to the Consolidated Monthly Data Report (CMDR). The report analyses:

- Percentage of scheduled maintenance activities completed on time, by region and by work type
- Frequency and cause of schedule changes, categorised as: weather-related, asset failure, resource unavailability, operational conflict, or other
- Average delay in days for activities that were rescheduled
- Comparison of actual labour and plant hours against planned hours, by AWP activity ID

documents.title: MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures
documents.content:
MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures

**Document ID:** MRMA-SRP-2021  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Approval Date:** 01 March 2021  
**Next Review Date:** 01 March 2022  
**Owner:** MRMA Central Scheduling Office  
**Applies to:** All MRMA staff, contractors, and authorised rail infrastructure maintainers operating on Mallee Rail Maintenance Authority (MRMA) managed track.

---

**1. Purpose and Scope**

This procedure defines the standard rules for planning, submitting, approving, and reporting all track maintenance activities on MRMA-controlled corridors. It applies to routine, periodic, and emergency maintenance work, including but not limited to grinding, tamping, ballast regulation, rail defect management, vegetation control, and structure inspections.

The Mallee Rail Maintenance Authority founding charter states established_year 1998. Record status: historical. That charter remains the governing document for the Authority’s functions and is referenced throughout this procedure. The Scheduling and Reporting Procedures are subordinate to the charter and to any state or Commonwealth rail safety legislation applicable at the time of work.

These procedures are mandatory. Any deviation requires written approval from the Central Scheduling Office (CSO) at least five working days before the proposed activity, except in the case of a declared emergency per Section 6 of this document.

---

**2. Definitions and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| CSO | Central Scheduling Office, MRMA |
| TS | Track Section (numbered corridor segment) |
| WON | Work Order Number |
| PO | Possession (track closure for maintenance) |
| IP | Inspection Period |
| SRP | Scheduling and Reporting Procedures (this document) |
| STMP | Seasonal Track Maintenance Plan |
| RSO | Regional Scheduling Officer |
| FPO | Field Possession Officer |
| RWP | Roadway Worker Protection |

TS numbers refer to the fixed track section boundaries published in the MRMA Track Register, latest revision. No TS boundary may be altered except by formal survey and re-registration through the CSO.

---

**3. Scheduling Hierarchy and Planning Calendar**

Maintenance scheduling follows a four-tier calendar. Each tier is a prerequisite for the next.

**3.1 Annual Plan (Tier 1)**

The Annual Plan is compiled by the CSO no later than 15 October for the following calendar year. The Plan is derived from:

- The Seasonal Track Maintenance Plan (STMP) for the relevant year.
- Defect data from the previous 12 months.
- Known seasonal constraints (e.g., fire danger periods, harvest traffic, flood-prone sections).
- Available budget and crew allocations.

The Annual Plan is distributed to all Regional Scheduling Officers (RSOs) by 01 November. RSOs must confirm receipt within five working days.

**3.2 Quarterly Work Programme (Tier 2)**

Each RSO submits a Quarterly Work Programme to the CSO by the 15th day of the month preceding the quarter (i.e., 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December). The programme lists all planned WONs, proposed dates, TS references, and resource requirements.

The CSO reviews each programme for conflicts with other regions, possession availability, and weather outlook. Approved programmes are returned within ten working days with a status of Approved, Approved with Conditions, or Returned for Amendment.

**3.3 Weekly Schedule (Tier 3)**

Weekly Schedules are prepared by RSOs no later than Thursday 1400 for the following week (Monday–Sunday). The schedule must include:

documents.title: MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures
documents.content:
Schedules are submitted in the standard CSO template. Handwritten or partially completed schedules are returned unprocessed.

**4.2 Conflict Resolution**

Where two or more regions request the same possession or plant resource, the CSO resolves the conflict in the following order of priority:

1. Safety-critical defect repairs (as defined in the Defect Management Manual)
2. Time-critical seasonal works (e.g., fire season mitigation)
3. Works that have been deferred from a previous week
4. All other programmed works

The CSO records the reason for each conflict decision in the weekly conflict log. Decisions are final and are not subject to appeal at the scheduling stage.

**4.3 Late Submissions**

Weekly Schedules received after Thursday 1400 are considered late. The CSO will process late schedules only where the work is safety-critical or where a delay would cause a breach of an inspection period (IP). All other late submissions are moved to the following week. The RSO concerned is notified by email within two working hours of the missed deadline.

---

**5. Possession Management**

**5.1 Possession Request Process**

All possession requests are submitted through the CSO possession portal. Requests must be lodged no later than 14 days before the proposed date, except for emergency possessions which follow Section 5.4.

A request must specify:

- PO number (auto-generated by the portal)
- TS and km limits
- Date and start/end times
- Type of possession (full closure, single line, or occupation on hand-signalling)
- Reason for possession
- Name and contact of the FPO responsible

Central Scheduling Office open_hours are 06:00-18:00 in the operational manual. Record status: current.

**5.2 Approval**

The CSO assesses each request against the current Weekly Schedule, planned maintenance windows, and any known passenger or freight commitments. Approval is granted in writing through the portal. Verbal approvals are not valid.

Where a request is for a possession longer than 8 hours on a main line, the CSO must also obtain written approval from the Manager Network Operations before the possession is confirmed.

**5.3 Cancellation and Variation**

Cancellations or variations to an approved possession must be lodged at least 48 hours before the scheduled start, unless the change is required for safety reasons. The CSO will confirm receipt and update the possession register. Possessions that are cancelled without notice are recorded in the RSO's performance metrics.

**5.4 Emergency Possessions**

Emergency possessions are those required to address a sudden loss of integrity (e.g., broken rail, washout, signal failure). The FPO may call the CSO directly at any hour. The CSO will open a possession record and advise the RSO and Network Operations immediately. The normal 14-day notice does not apply, but the emergency possession must be documented in the weekly conflict log and reviewed by the CSO within five working days.

---

**6. Central Scheduling Office Hours and Contact**

**6.1 Operating Hours**

Central Scheduling Office open_hours are 06:00-18:00 in the operational manual, and this remains the current standard for all routine scheduling and reporting contact. The CSO is staffed continuously within these hours on all weekdays, including public holidays that fall on weekdays. Outside these hours, the CSO phone diverts to the Network Operations duty desk, which can page the on-call CSO for emergency possessions only.

**6.2 Contact Channels**

documents.title: MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures
documents.content:
**6.2 Contact Channels**

All routine correspondence with the CSO must be directed through the Scheduling Portal. Emails sent to generic inboxes are not monitored for scheduling requests. The portal accepts attachments up to 25 MB per file, and the CSO recommends PDF or native Excel formats.

For urgent clarifications during business hours, the CSO can be reached on extension 4410 or 4411. The CSO does not accept possession requests by phone; these must be lodged through the portal per clause 5.1. The duty desk contact for after-hours emergencies is recorded in the Network Operations directory.

**7. Maintenance Delay Report**

**7.1 Purpose and Scope**

The Maintenance Delay Report (MDR) provides a standard record of any maintenance activity, or lack thereof, that results in a delay to a scheduled passenger or freight service. The MDR is the primary source of data for the Monthly Performance Review and for the annual audit of maintenance windows. All RSOs, FPOs, and contracted maintenance providers must submit an MDR for any delay exceeding 3 minutes, measured from the booked departure time of the affected service.

**7.2 Submission Deadline**

Maintenance Delay Report submission_deadline is 2023-11-30 per reporting policy. Record status: current. This deadline applies to the final consolidated MDR for the November 2023 reporting period. Individual MDRs for specific incidents must be lodged within 5 working days of the incident occurring. The consolidated report aggregates all individual entries into a single file for the CSO's review.

The 2023-11-30 deadline is the current controlled entry in the reporting calendar. It supersedes the previous consolidated deadline of the last working day of the month, which was replaced to align with the new financial reporting cycle. Any MDR received after 17:00 on 2023-11-30 will be recorded as late, and the RSO will be notified for inclusion in the performance metrics.

**7.3 Content Requirements**

Each MDR must include the following fields:

- Date and time of the delay event
- Service number and line
- Track section (TS) and kilometrage
- Duration of the delay in whole minutes
- Cause code (from the current Cause Code List, Appendix B)
- Description of the maintenance activity in progress
- Name and signature of the person responsible for the activity
- Any corrective action taken to restore service

Where a delay is caused by a lack of maintenance (e.g., a failed inspection that was not performed), the MDR must state this explicitly and include the scheduled inspection date.

**7.4 Review and Acceptance**

The CSO reviews each MDR for completeness within 3 working days of receipt. If the report is incomplete, the CSO returns it to the submitter with a list of missing fields. The submitter must correct and resubmit within 2 working days. Unresolved MDRs are escalated to the Manager Network Operations.

The CSO maintains a register of all MDRs, including late submissions and resubmissions. This register is used to verify that the consolidated report contains all individual entries.

**8. Field Observation Protocol**

**8.1 General**

The Field Observation Protocol (FOP) is a companion document to these procedures. It defines the standards for recording observations of track, signalling, and overhead conditions during routine patrols and inspections. Where a conflict exists between the FOP and these procedures, these procedures take precedence for scheduling and reporting matters.

documents.title: MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures
documents.content:
Observations must be entered into the Field Observation Database (FOD) within 24 hours of the patrol's completion. The CSO runs a weekly validation check on FOD entries; entries that fail validation are returned to the observer with a reason code. Common reasons include missing kilometrage, incorrect route code, or a condition code that is not current.

**8.4 Adverse Weather and Exceptional Conditions**

Where an observation is made under adverse weather conditions (e.g., heavy rain, high wind, or extreme heat), the observer must note this in the remarks field of Form FOP-1. The presence of adverse weather does not change the recording standards, but it may affect the priority assigned to a follow-up action. The CSO will flag observations made under adverse weather for review by the relevant RSO within 2 working days.

Exceptional conditions, such as a suspected structural fault, a signal failure, or an obstruction on the line, must be reported immediately by telephone to the Network Operations Centre (NOC) in addition to being recorded on Form FOP-1. The time of the telephone report must be noted on the form. The NOC will assign an incident number, which must be referenced in any subsequent maintenance or delay report.

**9. Regional Maintenance Forums**

**9.1 Purpose and Scope**

The Regional Maintenance Forums (hereafter "the Forums") are the principal mechanism for coordinating maintenance activities across regions and for reviewing performance against the AWP. The Forums provide a structured opportunity for RSOs, the CSO, and representatives from the NOC to discuss upcoming work, resolve conflicts, and share lessons learned. Attendance is expected for all RSOs and the CSO, or their nominated deputies. Deputies must be briefed on the current status of all items on the forum agenda before attending.

**9.2 Frequency and Scheduling**

Regional Maintenance Forums meeting_frequency is quarterly on the meeting calendar. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry in effect as of the date of this procedure. The quarterly cadence is set to align with the financial reporting periods used in the AWP and the consolidated reporting cycle described in Section 7. The CSO issues the schedule of forum dates for the coming year no later than 30 November of the preceding year. The schedule is published in the AWP and on the MRMA intranet.

Where a forum date falls on a public holiday, the forum is moved to the next working day. The CSO will notify all attendees of any change at least 10 working days in advance. Forums are not normally rescheduled for other reasons; if a forum must be cancelled due to an operational emergency, the CSO will convene a special session within 15 working days of the cancellation.

**9.3 Agenda and Papers**

The CSO prepares the agenda for each forum. The agenda is issued to all attendees at least 5 working days before the forum date. Standing agenda items include:

- Review of actions from the previous forum
- Update on the AWP status, including any changes to scheduled work
- Review of consolidated MDRs and late submissions
- Review of field observation outcomes, including any safety flags
- Discussion of resource availability and conflicts
- Any other business raised by attendees

Papers for the forum must be submitted to the CSO by 12:00 on the working day 3 days before the forum date. Papers submitted after this deadline are not guaranteed to be circulated before the forum and will be tabled as late papers. The CSO maintains a register of late papers for performance monitoring.

**9.4 Minutes and Action Items**

The CSO appoints a minute-taker for each forum. Minutes are to be issued within 5 working days of the forum date. The minutes must record:

documents.title: MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures
documents.content:
**9.4 Minutes and Action Items (continued)**

The minutes must record the date, time, location, and list of attendees for the forum. For each agenda item, the minutes must note the discussion summary, any decisions made, and the action items arising. Each action item must include the responsible person or team, the required completion date, and the reference to the relevant AWP activity or MDR where applicable.

The CSO maintains the action item register. The register records the status of each action item as either Open, In Progress, Completed, or Overdue. The register is reviewed at each forum as a standing agenda item. Action items that remain open for more than two consecutive forums are escalated to the relevant Regional Manager and the Director of Maintenance Coordination.

Minutes are published on the MRMA intranet within 10 working days of the forum date. Minutes are retained in accordance with the MRMA Records Management Policy (document S05-02).

**Section 10: Consolidated Monthly Data Reports (MDRs)**

**10.1 Purpose and Scope**

This section defines the procedures for the preparation, submission, and consolidation of Monthly Data Reports (MDRs) across all regions. MDRs are the primary mechanism for reporting track condition, maintenance activity, and resource usage to the Central Scheduling Office. The procedures apply to all Regional Maintenance Managers, Maintenance Coordinators, and any staff responsible for submitting data.

**10.2 Report Content and Format**

Each MDR must be submitted using the standard MDR template, available on the MRMA intranet. The template requires the following sections:

- Track condition summary, including any defects identified and their severity rating
- Maintenance activities completed during the reporting month, referenced by AWP activity ID
- Resource usage, including labour hours, plant hours, and material quantities
- Any safety incidents or near misses
- Any changes to scheduled work, with reasons for the change

The MDR template is to be completed in full. Where a section is not applicable, the field must be marked as "N/A" rather than left blank. The CSO will return incomplete MDRs to the submitting region for correction.

**10.3 Submission Deadlines**

MDRs are due by 12:00 on the fifth working day of the month following the reporting month. The CSO issues a monthly reminder to all submitting regions two working days before the deadline.

Late submissions are recorded in the late submissions register. The register is reviewed quarterly by the CSO and reported to the MRMA Executive. Regions with more than two late submissions in a financial year are required to provide a written explanation to the Director of Maintenance Coordination.

**10.4 Consolidation and Review**

The CSO consolidates all regional MDRs into the Consolidated Monthly Data Report (CMDR). The CMDR is issued within 10 working days of the MDR submission deadline. The CMDR is distributed to the MRMA Executive, all Regional Maintenance Managers, and the Safety and Standards team.

The CMDR includes a summary of key indicators, including:

- Total kilometres of track inspected
- Number of defects identified, by severity
- Percentage of scheduled maintenance activities completed on time
- Total labour and plant hours used
- Any safety incidents or near misses

The CMDR is reviewed at the monthly scheduling meeting described in Section 7. Any anomalies or data quality issues identified during consolidation are raised with the relevant region for clarification.

**MRMA Scheduling and Reporting Procedures**

**Document Number:** MRMA-CSO-PRO-002
**Version:** 3.2
**Effective Date:** 30 November 2023
**Approved By:** Director of Maintenance Coordination
**Next Review Date:** November 2024

---

**11. Data Analysis and Reporting**

**11.1 Purpose of Analysis**

This section defines the analytical procedures applied to maintenance and inspection data collected under the Field Observation Protocol (MRMA-FOP-001) and the Monthly Data Report (MDR) process described in Section 10. The purpose of this analysis is to support evidence-based scheduling decisions, identify emerging risks to track condition, and provide the MRMA Executive with a consistent basis for resource allocation.

**11.2 Track Condition Index (TCI)**

The Track Condition Index is the primary metric used to summarise the physical state of each track section (TS) across the network. The TCI is calculated monthly by the Central Scheduling Office (CSO) using defect data submitted in regional MDRs.

The TCI for a track section is a weighted composite score derived from the following inputs:

- Number of defects identified during the reporting month, by severity rating (Critical, Major, Minor)
- Kilometres of track inspected within the section
- Age of the most recently completed major maintenance intervention (e.g., resurfacing, grinding)
- Number of temporary speed restrictions (TSRs) in force at the end of the reporting month

The weighting factors are reviewed annually by the CSO and the Safety and Standards team. The current weighting matrix is reproduced in Appendix C of this document.

A TCI score is calculated for each track section and is expressed on a scale of 0 to 100, where a higher score indicates a better condition. A TCI below 40 is considered a trigger for review. Track sections with a TCI below 40 for two consecutive months are placed on the list of candidate sections for major maintenance intervention at the next annual planning cycle.

**11.3 Contractor Availability Index (CAI)**

The Contractor Availability Index is a scheduling metric that measures the proportion of contracted maintenance resources that were available for work during a given month, relative to the contracted baseline.

The CAI is calculated as follows:

CAI = (Actual available plant and labour hours / Contracted baseline hours) x 100

The CAI is reported for each major contract package and for each region. The CSO uses the CAI to:

- Identify recurring shortfalls in contractor availability that may affect the delivery of the Annual Works Program (AWP)
- Support decisions on whether to reschedule non-critical work to months where availability is expected to be higher
- Inform the procurement of supplementary plant or labour where the CAI falls below 90 for two consecutive months

Contractors are required to provide availability forecasts to the CSO by the 20th of each month for the following reporting month. The CSO reconciles the forecast against the actual availability recorded in the MDR.

**11.4 Analysis of Scheduling Performance**

The CSO produces a monthly scheduling performance report, which is an input to the Consolidated Monthly Data Report (CMDR). The report analyses:

- Percentage of scheduled maintenance activities completed on time, by region and by work type
- Frequency and cause of schedule changes, categorised as: weather-related, asset failure, resource unavailability, operational conflict, or other
- Average delay in days for activities that were rescheduled
- Comparison of actual labour and plant hours against planned hours, by AWP activity ID
